# lima: repairing a machine manager riddled with regressions, without a test suite

This is the command-line tool people use to describe, create and run local virtual machines, and it now gets a great many things wrong. Nothing about the configurations anyone writes changed and nothing about the guests changed, yet inputs that used to be accepted are now rejected, inputs that used to be rejected are now waved through, and operations that used to succeed now either fail outright or quietly hand back the wrong answer. The repository has received 29 separate undocumented edits. What follows is everything that has been observed to misbehave, described from the outside.

Checking a configuration someone wrote. A configuration listing two mount entries, one at a full path from the root and one beneath the home directory, now fails the checks that run when it is read, complaining about the mount location, even though both entries are written exactly as they always were; a mount location written relative to somewhere else is still turned away with its usual message about needing a full path from the root. In the same pass, a declared parameter that no provisioning script, probe, copy-to-host entry or forwarding entry ever mentions is quietly accepted, so the complaint that the parameter key is unused never appears at all, and it likewise fails to appear when the key is mentioned only under a differently capitalised spelling.
